results.name: Ledger identity holds for all seeded contracts; KR-001 closing = 45,000,000 KRW
Duplicate top-up (same content / same external ref / same txId) is rejected and balance is unchanged
Negative, zero, NaN, wrong-currency, unsupported-currency and over-precise amounts are rejected
Ledger is append-only: rows are frozen and corrections require a reasoned ADJUSTMENT
Reconciliation: MATCH / MINOR / MAJOR / UNCONFIRMED / CURRENCY_MISMATCH / stale
All five prepayment types exist in sample data and are ledger-capable
Refund > balance, future-dated, malformed date, consumption without period; confirmed-zero allowed only for consumption
Data separation by hotel / contract / entity / currency; cross-currency posting rejected
KPI exposure is grouped per currency and never summed across currencies
Average monthly consumption = mean of the last 3 CONFIRMED completed months
Zero consumption → "no consumption", no depletion date, no NaN/Infinity anywhere
Missing months are MISSING (not zero): partial → average of known months; none → NO_DATA & limit unavailable
Depletion date and velocity arithmetic (hand-computed)
Contract-expiry feasibility and estimated unused balance at expiry
Booking-date sales and PENDING consumption never drive the forecast; basis is explicit
Security deposits are NOT_APPLICABLE for consumption forecast / limit
Long-unconsumed detection (> 6 months of cover) and booking-sales trend
12 criteria, weights sum to 100, each with a rationale (KO+EN)
Unknown is excluded (not mid-scored): score unchanged, confidence reduced, unknown listed
Grade boundaries: exactly-at-threshold is inclusive; just below drops a grade
Red flags cap the grade regardless of score (score stays visible)
Low evidence: coverage < 50% → NR (despite a high raw score); 50–70% → capped at B
Unverified closure / news / AI claims never confirm a closure or cap the grade
Recoverability is a separate axis from credit grade
Rating history is preserved (append-only snapshots with reason and scores)
Hotel scale is A–D (+NR) and distinct from partner A–E; D/NR multipliers are zero
Grade multipliers A×2, B×1, C×0.5, D×0 on the 3-month average
Available top-up, projected exposure and exceed flag at the exact boundary
Already over limit: available 0, over-limit amount reported; any top-up requires approval
Extra safeguards: contract end, non-refundable, refund unknown, low recoverability
Holds: grade D/NR, critical/high alerts and consumption collapse zero the available top-up
Limit unavailable (no data / deposit) → simulation flags approval; never a number
Exact integer arithmetic for limits (floor, BigInt) incl. very large VND
Simulation is pure: no state mutation, writesLedger=false
Simulator rejects zero, negative, fractional and NaN requests
Seed produces the expected Critical / High / Medium alerts
Refund-overdue: past due & unpaid → alert; paid in full or not yet due → none; partial payment keeps it
Consumption collapse triggers at exactly −50% and not at −49.9%
Alert severity/enable are configuration-driven
Every alert carries hotel, title, detection date, evidence, action, SCM owner and status
Alert persistence: stable IDs, status survives re-detection, auto-clear keeps history, recurrence reopens
Rating drop ≥ 2 notches within 90 days raises a High alert; older history is ignored
Balance-confirmation Medium alerts: never confirmed or stale
Renewal delay (≤60 days to end, no renewal) and negative-balance High alert
CSV parser: quotes, escaped quotes, embedded commas/newlines, CRLF, BOM; unterminated quote errors
CSV validation: bad header, field count, currency, date, negative, unknown contract, long text, thousands separators
Duplicates inside one file and re-uploading the same file are caught; nothing is double-counted
CSV import: fatal errors leave ledger untouched; partial-bad files commit only valid rows
CSV export neutralises spreadsheet formulas; sample ledger CSV round-trips through the validator
Common weighted engine reproduces legacy compute() score and grade bit-for-bit on all 12 partners
RBAC: VIEWER cannot write anything; SCM/CEO/ADMIN limited to their permissions; denied attempts leave data unchanged and are audited
Audit log is hash-chained, records OK/REJECTED/DENIED, and detects tampering
approval packet and CEO review: complete packet, mock submit, CEO-only review with required feedback; ledger and balances never change; execution disabled
No code path can send data or run dynamic code: static scan of the prototype sources
No secrets / credentials / real-looking keys in the prototype tree
Reload consistency: state and every derived number are identical after a fresh load from storage
Corrupt / foreign storage is quarantined, never silently destroyed; legacy storage key is never touched
Stable unique IDs; every row ties to an existing hotel/contract; ledger rows carry currency + valid datetime
Hotel master & contract master carry every required field; owner unknown is explicit; brand ≠ legal counterparty
Configuration: validated, reason-required, audited with diff, recalculates grades; invalid sets rejected
AI is a labelled mock, cites source/date/confidence, cannot change amounts, grades or limits; contract extraction is heuristic
Recording a fact requires the verifier to be the signed-in user and an evidence reference
Regression: legacy OMH-NICE partner module is byte-identical to repo HEAD 9edba87 and computes the same 12 results
Hotel grades and partner grades are separate scales; the new app never imports or writes legacy state
All 7 screens render for every role in KO and EN without undefined/NaN/[object]/Infinity
Per-contract screens (profile with its top-up simulator, ledger, approval packet) render for all 20 contracts incl. NR / D / deposit / no-data cases, KO and EN
Dashboard filters (country/entity/currency/type) drive KPIs; empty filter combination yields empty state; control labels show currency & as-of date
Grade distribution counts hotels, not contracts: a hotel with several contracts is counted once at its lowest grade
Country card: the prepayment balance is shown as a total split into prebuy, hard block and other, in the one currency of the country
Commit RN and Commit Rev are two prepayment types: filtered apart, and each has its own line in the balance next to prebuy and hard block
XSS: hostile text from CSV / notes / names is HTML-escaped everywhere it is rendered
Read-only roles see disabled controls; writers see enabled ones
Performance: 208-contract portfolio computes < 2 s; 2,000-row CSV validates + commits < 3 s; no state growth on recompute
Math robustness: BigInt-safe on very large amounts; no float drift on repeated postings
Duplicate detection survives case, width, zero-width and time-zone variants of the same transaction
Reconciliation compares the ledger AS OF the hotel confirmation date; later legitimate postings do not create a false MAJOR
Real people whose names start with "Ai"/"Bot"/"Auto" can verify; service-account names cannot
Facts: whitelisted keys, evidence mandatory, no deletion (superseded with history), counterparty status needs evidence
Config validation covers every section; a rejected/failed change can never brick the app; all-or-nothing rollback
Prototype keys and unknown IDs are rejected everywhere (no pollution, no phantom state)
Storage write failure rolls the command back: memory never diverges from what is persisted
Loading validates ledger rows and config: corrupt amounts are quarantined instead of silently inflating balances
One confirmed-zero month with two unknown months is NOT "no consumption": no depletion claim, no expiry alert, no refund classification
Alert lifecycle: dismissed alerts reopen on recurrence, manual RESOLVED with a persisting condition is reopened, dismissals are disclosed in the approval packet
Contracts with a balance but no computable limit are counted as "limit unknown" (not silently ignored)
Consumption period must be a real, plausible month; timezone is mandatory; absurd amounts and balance overflow are rejected
Segregation of duties: the creator of a review request cannot review it, and the review needs feedback; malformed arguments are denied by RBAC first; huge requests rejected
Loading replays every ledger row through the posting validator: currency/contract/uniqueness/opening/refund/date tampering is quarantined
A broken audit chain is surfaced (AUDIT_BROKEN) without destroying the data
The 'provisional' flag cannot be cleared by an administrator (only a CEO-approved release may)
Service-style verifier names (automation, aibot, svc-*, gpt-*, claude…) cannot verify facts; human names still can
CSV export neutralises formula injection incl. leading whitespace, tab/CR and full-width operators; negative numbers stay numeric
Duplicate guard covers reference-vs-no-reference postings of one transaction (manual + CSV) but keeps genuinely different references distinct
Reconciliation cut-off uses the transaction instant in the business day (KST), not the offset it was written in
A critical alert backed by a verified fact cannot be dismissed, and the top-up hold follows the fact itself
Verified facts: only an evidenced retraction by a different person can lift them; unverified or same-person replacement is refused
Hotel-level cap: it can only hold the limit lower; raising or lifting needs the CEO or an admin; every change is audited, kept in history, never touches the ledger and is checked on load

Data-driven scores: every criterion is read off the data by a fixed rule (cover months, refund clause, collateral share, reconciliation, refund record, country table, verified entity, recorded ownership); missing data is Unknown and names what would settle it
Nobody types a score: no command sets one, stored data carries none, the same data gives the same scores for every user, and opinions never move the score
Recording the data the scores read: ownership status, refund clause and collateral need the signed-in person and an evidence reference, are audited and kept in history, and move the score
Scoring settings: validated, audited, and a change recalculates every hotel
A local entity holds its own currency only (Korea KRW, Japan JPY, Vietnam VND); the Singapore head office may hold any; stored data that breaks this is quarantined

Registering a hotel and its contract: ids and the opening ledger row are made by the command, every input is validated, nothing is left behind when it is refused, only SCM and admin may do it, and the stored result reloads clean
Registering a Commit RN or a Commit Rev contract: both are accepted as two separate types; the same type twice is refused

Record stopped and long-held deposit alerts (from the Japan SCM file): a balance with no ledger record for N days, a deposit held for N years; deposits are not stale, zero balances never alert, parameters and switches work

Balance concentration alert (from the Japan SCM file): a contract holding a large share of its country and currency group raises it; it needs a group of at least three, deposits form their own group, and it can be dismissed

A hard block paid and settled month by month has no balance to consume: no consumption-based limit, no consumption score, a hold reason of its own; the registration accepts the flag for hard blocks only
Refunds that came back with no delay on record lift the settlement-history score to 4 (the Japan ledger shows returned deposits and no late refund); an overdue request still scores 1
Load check: approvals and dismissed alerts recorded in storage must be backed by an audit entry
Config: unknown keys and out-of-range values are rejected
Integration-status text and key hold reasons exist in both languages
Hostile strings posted through commands are escaped in every view (regression guard for the escaping)
Duplicates: period/status on non-consumption rows and exotic minus/invisible characters do not create a second transaction
Load check v2: forged approval status/packet/contract, re-dismissal, historical-flag escape, duplicate ids and audit truncation are all flagged
Very slow consumption never yields an overflowed "NaN" date; version is locked; integration names are bilingual
Scale: 20,000-row ledger computes < 3 s and loads < 6 s; indexed and unindexed posting agree; running balances equal a full recomputation
Load check v3: approval replay after reset, and edits to ledger/facts/ratings/config made outside the commands are detected
References: variation selectors and other default-ignorable code points are ignored when comparing
Test-suite hygiene: BigInt path is exercised with amounts beyond double precision
Language packs cover every UI string (ja, vi) and contain no stale keys
Translations keep placeholders, leading/trailing spaces and untranslatable tokens; no Korean left; scripts look right
LF templates fill every placeholder; language switching is validated and persisted by the core
All screens render in Japanese and Vietnamese for every role: no missing translations, no leftover Korean labels, no unfilled placeholders
Japanese and Vietnamese key terms are used consistently (glossary check)
hotel code normalisation and decimal-to-minor conversion
month windows respect the 30-day limit and the fixture enforces the same rules as the tool
collect pages through more than one page and totals match the source exactly
an incompletely paged result is flagged truncated and refused, never totalled
call validation: wrong basis, long window, bad hotel code and non-booking tools are refused
duplicates, rows without ids, rows outside the window and wrong-hotel rows are not counted
currencies stay separate; decimals, cancelled rows, restricted and unusable amounts are handled without guessing
the snapshot keeps aggregates only: no guest, booking or seller references
snapshot validation rejects tampering and malformed content
covered months: adjacent windows merge, partial months do not count, empty covered month means zero
hotel mapping: ELLIS-<code> and plain codes match, duplicates and missing ids are reported, unknown hotels are dropped
import command: permission, audit, only matched hotels stored, ledger and balances untouched
preview is a dry run: same rules, no state change, no audit row
import rejects a repeat, an older snapshot and a snapshot with no known hotel; a newer one replaces the older
real ELLIS data never enters the sample state and sample data never enters a real one
comparison statuses: match, tolerance edge, zero cases, missing months, currency mismatch, stale, deposits
stored ELLIS data is integrity-checked on load: edited amounts, forged imports and malformed sections are caught
the synthetic sample is valid, fully synthetic, and shows each comparison case it is meant to demonstrate
the integration panel reports the snapshot adapter honestly and the tool contract lists only what is implemented
a large snapshot (50 hotels x 36 months) validates, imports and compares quickly
a month that was only partly collected is "not collected", never a false divergence
unknown fields are refused wherever they appear; nothing outside the schema is stored
time stamps must be real and carry a zone; equal or unreadable times never count as newer
a window in which rows were dropped before their month was known is not "covered"
covered months must be provable from complete hotel-level pulls inside the window
the fingerprint does not depend on key order, so a re-ordered copy is recognised as the same snapshot
negative amounts (refunds, adjustments) are skipped and flagged, never netted into a month
cancel detection is anchored; stored ELLIS data must match the state kind and its import history
bookings in other currencies are converted through the booking-time KRW rate and marked as converted
months outside the contract period are not compared; a month holding the start or end cannot be split
two contracts at one hotel: same currency is shared (not compared), different currencies never take each other's bookings
NET needs the revenue; when it is hidden the default basis reports incomplete and BILLING still works
review regressions in the comparison: shared hotels are decided per month, unjudged contracts are not OK, same-currency mode counts only own bookings, the tolerance is exact
a snapshot whose KRW figures disagree with the original-currency figures is refused
second review: the KRW equivalent of revenue is checked too, tiny amounts may round to 0 KRW, and the tolerance option is validated
hotel scope (the tracker definition): no clipping to the contract period, no shared-hotel skipping, every currency converted; contract scope stays the default
check-out basis: bookings go to the month they check out in, the pull uses CHECK_OUT_DATE, and one snapshot never mixes bases
a contract that starts mid-month is compared on the since-start aggregate of that month, and only then
a forged or inconsistent since-start aggregate is refused
the snapshot keeps KRW equivalents; a non-KRW booking without a rate is skipped and flagged; the new fields are validated
accounts: every role has one, ids are unique, passwords are checked exactly, odd names never match
before login nothing can be read-modified: every command is refused and the refusal is audited as anonymous
the role comes from the account: callers cannot pick or raise it
a failed login is audited without the password, says the same for unknown and wrong, and opens nothing
five wrong passwords lock that name for 30 seconds, also for unknown names; other names are not affected
logout ends the session, is audited, and everything is refused afterwards
a login expires after 8 hours; a stored login is restored only if it is genuine, and its role is looked up again
login and logout rows keep the audit chain and the stored state valid across a reload
separation of duties through accounts: SCM drafts and submits, only the CEO account decides
the permission table: matrix agrees with can(), every permission has a label, only the CEO role decides approvals
the app has no role switcher and does not use the test hook; it starts logged out
cell parsing: dates in the formats PICs use, amounts with separators and brackets, and what is unreadable
columns are found by their heading text: any order, hidden or extra columns, title rows, guidance and example rows
arrangement types: the five of the system map plus Commit RN and Commit Rev as two types (Hybrid counts as Commit Rev); blanks and unknown names are reported and not converted
input checks on the synthetic sample: each built-in problem is found, the healthy row is clean
every threshold of the checks: confirmation age, mismatch size, ending, long unused, no booking, over-funded, planned top-up
the converted ledger passes the system import rules and ends on the tracker balance
top-up log: rows inside the window become ledger rows, older ones fold into the opening; bad rows are refused; a missing log is flagged
blank usage is unknown, not zero; a derived opening that would be negative is refused instead of invented
risk register: yes/no columns, example row skipped, evidence and open disputes noted
the unified CSV files: layouts, formula-injection safety, commas and line breaks in text, and the contract fields of the system
preview command: SCM/Admin only, changes nothing, rejects oversized input, uses the state as-of date
command-line tool: real data may not be written into the project; exit codes; files written outside
review regressions: usage columns must be readable, distinct and past; blocking is per sheet and per hotel; negative opening or usage converts nothing; ambiguous log rows are refused
second review: no-usage arrangements, month names, ordering, duplicates, field limits, minor/major units and the rest
the tracker Usage is sales production, not the deducted amount: every converted consumption row says so and the check list carries one note
the shipped sample is synthetic and identical in both copies; no real-looking ids or names
next check date: the 1st of next month; a D / NR grade or a live critical / high alert is looked at again within 7 days
top-up timing: depletion date minus the lead time, urgency, hold, and the cases without a date
the speed comes from ELLIS when the ledger has none, and both speeds are shown with their gap
ELLIS outlook: last completed months as compared, plus the stays already on the books for this and later months
cooperation recommendation: continue, continue with conditions, undecided, wind down, with the reasons that fired
every sample contract gets a plan and an opinion; nothing is written to the ledger
an offset reduces the balance, needs a reason, cannot exceed the balance, and keeps the identity
an offset is not consumption: forecast, average usage and refund tracking ignore it
CSV import and the store accept offsets with the same rules, and permissions are those of ledger entry
planned top-up: checked against the limit on the view, carried into the approval packet, never written to the ledger
